Title: Four workers hit by train in Japan
Article:
TOKYO: Four people were unconscious in Japan on Thursday after being hit by a train, authorities said, with one media report saying they were "without vital signs."
The incident involving four workers took place at Shin-Kanuma Station north of Tokyo, the fire department said.
"When emergency services arrived, three workers were still trapped under the train, while one was on the platform," a fire department spokesman told AFP.
"Before being taken to hospital, all four of them were unconscious," he added.
Emergency services were first called at 10.47am (0147 GMT).
Nippon TV reported that the workers were removing weeds from around the train track and that all were "without vital signs."
Japanese railways have one of the best safety records in the world, with fatal accidents extremely rare due to high levels of maintenance and training, and use of advanced technology.
Famously there has never been a passenger fatality from a derailment or a collision on Japan's network of "shinkansen" bullet trains.--AFP

Title: Immigration lorry driver charged with causing death of three family members in crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An Immigration Department lorry driver today claimed trial at the magistrates' court here to five charges, including three counts of causing death by reckless or dangerous driving in connection with yesterday's fatal crash at the Maju Junction intersection.
Mohd Akbar Zainol, 43, pleaded not guilty when the charges were read to him before magistrate Aliaa Anwar.
He was charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 with causing the deaths of Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaik Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Norshazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12.
The three family members died after the lorry allegedly crashed into a Proton Saga before losing control and hitting four pedestrians at the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection at 1am yesterday.
Akbar was also charged under Section 43(1) of the same Act with driving without due care and attention, resulting in injuries to pedestrian Nor Hayati Rozali.
The fifth charge, under Section 79(2) of the Act, alleged that he failed to obey a red traffic light at the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection.

Title: Saarani: Ex-aide quit over health reasons, no speculation over drug claims
Article:
IPOH: Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad today said no assumptions should be made over social media claims that his former political secretary, Mohamad Hamidi Baharuddin, was involved in drugs.
Saarani said Mohamad Hamidi had resigned from the post, effective Aug 17, citing health reasons.
"He wrote a letter to me dated Aug 10, stating that he wanted to resign, effective Aug 17. So, we accepted it.
"He gave health reasons, saying he needed time to seek treatment," he told reporters after launching Invest in Perak Day 2026 at a hotel here, today.
Saarani was responding to questions about claims circulating on social media that Mohamad Hamidi was involved in drugs.
"I have also read that on social media. As long as there is no evidence from the authorities, whether regarding his health or from the police, I do not want to make any assumptions," he said.
Asked about Mohamad Hamidi's replacement, Saarani said the appointment would be made in due course.
"We will appoint a replacement in due course," he said.
A Facebook user, Zaharin Mohd Yasin, posted a status claiming that Mohamad Hamidi had resigned after he allegedly revealed that the political secretary was a drug addict.
Mohamad Hamidi had served as Saarani's political secretary since January 2023. He is also the Umno Youth chief of the Lenggong division.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khalid rejects 'dead horse' jibe over Tabung Haji RCI
Article:
KOTA BARU: Amanah has dismissed a political leader's claim that the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji was merely "flogging a dead horse", saying the issues raised remain relevant and require action.
Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad said the RCI should not be dismissed as a futile exercise as it had highlighted alleged irregularities, corruption and abuse of power.
"A political party leader recently said the RCI is flogging a dead horse.
"What is the point of beating a horse that is already dead? Even if we beat it, it cannot get up and it will not move.
"But actually, the horse is not dead. This concerns corruption, abuse of power and wrongdoing. It will always be relevant when such cases are exposed and action needs to be taken," he said.
[[nid:1515116]]
Khalid, who is Kemubu Agricultural Development Authority (Kada) chairman, said this after launching Kada's Merdeka Month and Jalur Gemilang 2026 flag-raising ceremony here today.
He said exposing and preventing wrongdoing was necessary to uphold good governance and prevent abuse of power from becoming entrenched in politics.
"We want to be the best ummah, so we must uphold what is right and prevent wrongdoing.
"In preventing wrongdoing, for example, there is the case involving Tabung Haji, where the RCI revealed irregularities and wrongdoings that caused TH to suffer losses amounting to billions of ringgit," he said.
Khalid said that once the RCI report was made public, the Attorney-General should review its findings and take appropriate legal action against those found responsible.
"The Attorney-General should study the RCI report again and take action, including prosecuting those found guilty.
"This is part of the effort to prevent wrongdoing because if abuse of power occurs and we allow it to continue, it will eventually become a culture in our politics," he said.
His remarks referred to the RCI into Tabung Haji, which examined alleged irregularities and governance issues involving the Islamic pilgrimage fund.
Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan lawmakers have also called for a new RCI to investigate the management and operations of TH.
On Tuesday,
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim
said investigations into issues surrounding TH were not confined to the period covered by the RCI and could extend beyond 2020, including developments up to 2025.
He said the RCI served as the main framework for examining issues involving TH, but enforcement agencies were not restricted from investigating matters that occurred before or after the period covered by the commission.

Title: KL-Karak widening project to be completed one year ahead of schedule
Article:
GOMBAK: The RM2.1 billion Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway widening project is expected to be completed in 2029, a year ahead of schedule, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said.
He said the project was originally scheduled for completion in 2030 under its four-year construction contract, but AFA Prime Bhd had assured that the works could be completed by 2029.
The project, fully funded by AFA Prime, involves widening 45.3 kilometres of the KL-Karak between Gombak and Bentong, as well as constructing a 999-metre third tunnel at Genting Sempah.
"That is very encouraging because it means the project will be completed ahead of time," he said at the groundbreaking ceremony for the third Genting Sempah tunnel and launch of the KL-Karak widening project today.
"This is not simply about building a bigger tunnel. It is about closing the gap between east and west, between potential and opportunity, and between what exists and what the people on the East Coast deserve."
Nanta said the highway would be widened from three to four lanes between Gombak and Genting Sempah, while the stretch between Genting Sempah and Bentong would be widened from two to three lanes.
Physical works began in March this year, with the project expected to improve traffic flow, road safety and travelling comfort along the key east-west corridor.
The new 999-metre tunnel will be constructed using the New Austrian Tunnelling Method (NATM), which Nanta said was more suitable for the physical conditions of the site.
The project comes as traffic along the KLK has increased significantly from about 41,000 vehicles daily in 1997 to more than 135,000 vehicles currently.
Nanta said the government is also taking broader measures to improve road safety and reduce traffic accidents and fatalities nationwide.
"Road safety is not only about this particular location. Recently, we had a Cabinet committee meeting, or Cabinet Action Council, specifically on road congestion and safety chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
"A lot was discussed on how we can reduce accidents and fatalities. According to the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research, the number is very high in our country with 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents nationwide.
"That is very high. That is why the government is serious about reducing road accidents and the loss of lives," he said.
On toll rates, Nanta said there would be no immediate increase following completion of the project.
"It's not immediate. There will be an increase later, but we do not know when yet. The terms are provided for in the contract, but there will be no increase in the next two or three years," he added.

Title: Telcos must explain excessive prepaid line registrations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil will ask telecommunications companies (telcos) to explain allegations that excessive numbers of prepaid lines are being registered under individuals' names and potentially misused for scams.
Fahmi said he took note of concerns raised by Muslim Consumers Association of Malaysia (PPIM) chief activist Datuk Nadzim Johan, including claims that people had discovered numerous phone lines registered under their names without their knowledge.
"I will look into this matter. I have requested some information so that we can take action.
"If it is true, the telcos will have some explaining to do.
"I will call the telco CEOs to meet me and provide a full explanation on this matter," he said.
Fahmi said the government had already introduced several safeguards, including requiring prepaid line registrations to be verified using MyDigital ID.
He said the measures were important as the government had found that some registered phone numbers were eventually used for malicious purposes.
"Sometimes foreigners misuse them, sometimes unidentified people, and there are also people who hand over their MyKad and so on," he said.
Fahmi was speaking at the launch of the National Anti-Scam Awareness campaign organised by PPIM.
Nadzim alleged that telcos were partly responsible for the proliferation of scam cases by allowing large numbers of lines to be registered under a single individual's name.
He cited a case involving a 70-year-old man who discovered that 18 phone lines had been registered under his name despite having only one line.
Nadzim also said that PPIM had received information involving up to 400 lines registered under a single name, which were subsequently sold to scammers.
He said that some people could also face financial repercussions, including adverse credit records, when bills for unauthorised lines registered under their names went unpaid.
Nadzim called for greater accountability from the telecommunications industry, saying stronger action was needed to prevent phone lines from being exploited by scam syndicates.

Title: Kedah police open 69 disciplinary probes involving 90 personnel this year
Article:
ALOR STAR: Kedah police have opened 69 disciplinary investigation papers involving 90 policemen, personnel and civilian staff this year for alleged misconduct, including criminal offences, corruption, drug-related offences, traffic violations and Syariah offences.
Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said the figure was lower than the 155 investigation papers opened last year involving similar offences.
He said the 2025 cases involved 39 senior police officers, 248 junior policemen and seven civilian personnel.
"This year, 11 senior police officers, 76 junior police personnel and three civilian staff are being investigated.
"Of the cases opened, 33 involved criminal offences, four commercial offences, three Syariah offences, seven corruption cases and 24 drug-related offences," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after the flag-off ceremony for the 69th National Day flag-waving programme at the Kedah police contingent headquarters here today.
Adzli said the Kedah police had taken disciplinary action against policemen through suspension from duty, interdiction and dismissal from 2021 to date.
He said 67 personnel had been suspended from duty during the period, involving 25 drug cases, 19 criminal cases, 16 cases involving the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), three Syariah cases and two misconduct cases.
"Ten policemen were suspended from duty between 2023 and 2026, comprising two senior officers and eight junior personnel.
"The cases involved one criminal offence, one Syariah offence, five drug-related offences, two MACC cases and one traffic offence," he said.
Adzli said 10 personnel were dismissed between 2025 and June this year, involving senior police officers and civilian personnel in one Syariah case, two drug cases, three MACC cases and four misconduct cases.
He said there was a misconception that suspension from duty was a form of punishment for police personnel facing disciplinary proceedings.
"People often say that when police officers are involved in misconduct, we protect our own and, at most, transfer them elsewhere.
"I want to stress that suspension from duty is not a punishment. It is an initial measure to prevent and stop an individual from continuing the misconduct.
"If an officer was involved in robbery or extortion, we must transfer them to a division where they have no access to the public," he said.
Adzli said investigations would continue even after an officer was transferred, and prosecution would be pursued once sufficient evidence was obtained.
He stressed that the Kedah police would not protect any officer or personnel found to have committed disciplinary or other offences.
"Most of those who have been subjected to disciplinary action are relatively young, up to 50 years old. They include a deputy superintendent involved in a fatal accident in Perak several years ago and an officer involved in a rape case in Kuala Muda last year," he said.

Title: Meta trial rocked by claim safety tools were 'designed to fail'
Article:
OAKLAND: A former employee testified on Wednesday that some of Meta's safety tools for Facebook and Instagram were "designed to fail," contradicting the company's defence strategy in a landmark trial in California.
For a second day, Meta is fending off accusations by a coalition of US states that it deliberately designed its products to hook children and gather their data while misleading the public.
A loss for the social media giant could see it slapped with a US$200 billion penalty, force fundamental changes to its business model and send shockwaves through the industry.
Meta doesn't deny that some users, including teens, have negative experiences on its two core apps, but the company maintains it created features to reduce those risks.
"There can be no dispute that Meta has both recognised that people can struggle with their use of social media and tried to come up with tools to help them," Meta's lawyer, Paul Schmidt, said on Tuesday during opening statements.
However, Meta made some of those tools opt-in, meaning that users had to intentionally turn them on, including a feature launched in 2021 called "Take a Break," which lets users set reminders to take breaks from scrolling on Instagram.
"In my experience, 'Take a Break' is a feature that's designed to fail," Arturo Bejar, a former Meta engineering director, testified on the second day of a trial that is expected to last around six weeks.
Bejar is the first witness to take the stand and has argued that the company prioritised profits over safety by encouraging people to spend more and more time on Facebook and Instagram.
That strategy led to decisions like making safety features optional, including tools designed to combat endless scrolling or limit enticing notifications.
"Notifications are built and designed in order to bring people back, so they spend more time and get more revenue. They're not designed for mental health... or the safety of the person," Bejar said on Wednesday.
Days before the trial, Meta attempted to block Bejar from testifying, a move that the judge denied.
- 'BIG TOBACCO MOMENT' -
Many experts have called this trial social media's "big tobacco moment," referring to a blockbuster settlement between tobacco companies in the United States and dozens of states in the 1990s, which led to billions of dollars in penalties and changes to how products were marketed.
Similarly, dozens of states are once again intervening where "Congress failed to act," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said Tuesday afternoon.
The tobacco and social media cases both involve "public health, and in some cases, marketing to kids that hurt kids," Weiser continued.
During opening statements on Tuesday, California prosecutor Megan O'Neill painted Meta's business model as one intended to "hook the users, hold them for as long as they can, harvest their data, and then hide the truth from the public."
Meta "exploited how kids' brains work," O'Neill said.
Founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Instagram head Adam Mosseri are among the star witnesses expected to testify, according to court documents.
However, during a press conference Tuesday afternoon, California Attorney General Rob Bonta declined to confirm whether Zuckerberg would be called to the stand.
Before the trial began, the company denied the allegations, insisting it had worked with parents, experts and law enforcement to incorporate safeguards for children.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM7.93m drug haul: Nine nabbed after police bust raft house stash
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A floating raft house in Masai was allegedly used by a drug syndicate as a storage hub before police busted the operation, arresting nine suspects and seizing drugs worth RM7.93 million.
The syndicate, believed to have been operating since January, allegedly used the raft house to store drugs, while another house was used to process ecstasy pills.
Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said the arrests followed three raids in Masai and Ulu Tiram on Aug 12, which led to the arrest of the syndicate's 54-year-old mastermind.
"In the first raid at a house in Masai, three men were arrested and various types of drugs were seized.
"Two machines used to process ecstasy pills and equipment for repackaging the drugs were also seized.
"In the second raid at the raft house, four men, including the mastermind, were arrested and more drugs were seized.
"The third raid was conducted at a house in Ulu Tiram, where a couple was arrested with drugs," he told a press conference at the Johor police contingent headquarters here today.
Hoo said investigations found that each suspect had a specific role in the syndicate.
"The first suspect was a runner and the second was his assistant.
"The third was the storekeeper responsible for preparing 'drug juice', while the fourth was the mastermind.
"The fifth was a boat mechanic, the sixth and seventh were caretakers of the raft house, while the eighth was involved in processing ecstasy pills. The ninth suspect, a foreign woman, was his girlfriend," he said.
Among the drugs seized were 40.381kg of MDMA powder, 23.869kg of ecstasy powder, 23,025 Erimin 5 pills, 0.574kg of methamphetamine, 4.91kg of ketamine, 18.40 litres of liquid ketamine and 230 cartridges of liquid methamphetamine.
The drugs were estimated to be worth RM7.93 million and could have been used by up to 323,841 users.
Police also seized five cars, two speedboats and RM11,320 in cash.
Hoo said preliminary urine screening found all nine suspects, aged between 35 and 60, tested positive for methamphetamine.
"Checks on their previous records found that six of the suspects had past drug-related offences.
"All suspects have been remanded until Aug 25," he added.

Title: Immigration lorry driver arrives in court over fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  The Immigration Department lorry driver involved in the fatal crash along Jalan Sultan Ismail yesterday arrived at the magistrates' court here today under heavy police escort.
The 43-year-old suspect arrived at 12pm, escorted by several police officers into the courtroom.
He is expected to be charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 in connection with the crash, which claimed the lives of three members of the same family.
The
suspect was detained
to assist investigations following the crash at the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection early Wednesday morning.
The crash occurred when the Immigration Department lorry, believed to have entered the intersection against a red traffic light, collided with a Proton Saga before hitting four pedestrians and an Inokom Matrix.
Three victims died in the incident, while another family member was injured and taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for treatment.

Title: Zambry: Independent committee to draft new law after Auku repeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An independent committee will be established to engage stakeholders and determine the framework for a new legislation to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) following its repeal.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the repeal would require several immediate measures, including a transitional legal mechanism to prevent a regulatory void as Auku currently serves as the principal law governing public universities.
"The first step is to establish an independent committee to examine, execute, and look into all aspects of the new legislation.
"If Auku is repealed immediately without a replacement, how will our universities function?
"Without an overarching legal framework, universities cannot operate.
"Thus, a transitional legal mechanism must be put in place while we work on the new bill, ensuring that institutional operations run smoothly after the act is repealed," he told reporters after launching the Graduate Employability Strategic Plan 2026–2030 here today.
Zambry said the reform process comprises four key steps: forming the independent committee, holding extensive stakeholder engagement, establishing a dedicated drafting team to formulate the new Bill, and executing the transitional mechanism.
He did not specify a deadline for the rollout, noting that the legislation requires thorough consultation.
Zambry said that Auku is an umbrella law comprising 44 sections, of which only seven directly concern student activities, while the remainder govern university establishment, governance, academic freedom, and administration.
He added that higher education governance also intersects with several other statutes, including the Educational Institutions (Discipline) Act 1976, the Statutory Bodies (Discipline and Surcharge) Act 2000 , and the Private Higher Educational Institutions Act 1996 , which require legislative harmonisation.
Zambry said repealing Auku was in line with the ministry's long-term plan to introduce a single, comprehensive "One Higher Education Act", as outlined in the Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035.
He acknowledged long-standing concerns regarding student and academic freedom under the current act, reiterating the government's commitment to creating a progressive and future-proof legislative framework.
"After 50 years of Auku, and given the dynamic evolution of our higher education landscape, we must review the framework comprehensively across all dimensions," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Breakthrough' mRNA cancer drug cuts melanoma recurrence in major trial
Article:
WASHINGTON: US drugmakers Merck and Moderna said Wednesday a personalised cancer treatment had shown success in reducing the recurrence of melanoma tumors in a late-stage trial hailed by experts as a "breakthrough."
The news sent shares in Moderna soaring 145 percent to US$154 while Merck's stock was up more than 12 percent to US$152.
The drug, called "intismeran autogene," is based on the same messenger RNA (mRNA) technology behind Covid-19 vaccines.
Researchers have for years been trying to apply mRNA treatments against cancer, but this was the first time such a drug showed positive results in a large, late-stage clinical trial.
"Today marks an extraordinary milestone for Moderna, for mRNA science and, most importantly, for patients with cancer," Moderna CEO Stephane Bancel said in a statement.
The trial lasted approximately a year and involved 1,137 patients who, following surgical removal of their cancers, were randomised into groups, with two-thirds receiving the new treatment plus pembrolizumab – the current standard-of-care drug – while the rest received pembrolizumab alone.
The companies said they would present their data at an upcoming international conference and begin filings with regulators for approval.
- 'PROOF OF PRINCIPLE' -
Lennard Lee, an oncologist and assistant professor at the University of Oxford who was not involved in the trial, called the results "very encouraging," adding: "We should now look forward to seeing the complete data."
Oncologist Marco Gerlinger, a professor at London's Barts Cancer Institute, added that beyond being good news for patients with melanoma, it was "proof of principle that personalised cancer vaccines work."
"I think it is fair to call it a breakthrough in the development of new cancer immunotherapies," he added, while also noting the press release was short on details.
The treatment works by taking a sample of the patient's tumour and identifying its unique mutational signature, or "fingerprint," then using mRNA technology to fight it.
Messenger RNA technology uses synthetic molecular instructions encased in tiny fat bubbles that temporarily enter cells, causing them to produce targets that train the body's immune system.
The technology was first conceived decades ago but came to the fore during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Moderna and Pfizer developed vaccines that were highly effective against serious forms of the illness.
Melanoma is one of the deadliest forms of skin cancer, with more than 330,000 new cases diagnosed worldwide in 2022.
"Together with Merck, we are now studying intismeran in combination with pembrolizumab and other anti-cancer therapies, and as a monotherapy, across multiple tumor types and stages of disease, including melanoma, lung, bladder and kidney cancers," said Bancel.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Factory supervisor arrested over upside-down Jalur Gemilang, Johor flag
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police arrested a factory supervisor yesterday after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag were found flying upside down at a factory in Gelang Patah here.
The factory is located in the Southern Industrial and Logistics Clusters (SILC) area.
Acting district police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya@Yahaya said the 56-year-old Malaysian admitted to putting up the flags on Tuesday, but told police the upside-down display was accidental.
He said police received a report the next day and inspected the premises.
"Checks found 3 flagpoles in front of the premises, with one Jalur Gemilang and one Johor flag flown upside down.
"The supervisor was detained and both flags were seized," he said in a statement today.
Saifullah said the case was being investigated under Section 5 of the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act 1963, Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 and Section 505(b) of the Penal Code.
Earlier, Kota Iskandar assemblyman
Datuk Pandak Ahmad
alerted the authorities after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag were found displayed upside down.
The premises was ordered to close, while further checks by the Iskandar Puteri City Council found that the factory was
operating without a valid
business licence.

Title: Balancing independence, cooperation in middle power politics
Article:
LETTERS:
On July 21, eight Democratic members of the US Congress wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the suspension of International Military Education and Training funding to Malaysia unless Putrajaya reversed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive to deport Israeli nationals holding dual citizenship.
Three weeks later, on Aug 13, a White House report on transhipment placed Malaysia in its second tier of economies accused of laundering Chinese exports to evade US tariffs.
Both arrived against the backdrop of a 19 per cent US reciprocal tariff on Malaysian imports, a rate subsequently retained under the Malaysia-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade signed in October 2025, with exemptions for 1,711 tariff lines.
None of these severed the relationship. Malaysian exports to the United States rose by 17.2 per cent in 2025 to RM233.1 billion, driven largely by electrical and electronic products; the two military forces continued to train together; and officials from both capitals remained at the table.
Historically, Washington recognised the Federation of Malaya on Aug 31, 1957. Sixty-nine years later, the durability of the relationship does not depend on Malaysia choosing the United States over China. It depends on accepting that Malaysia will hedge its bets between the two superpowers.
The United States and China are not rivals to be ranked but two ends of one production line: sever either, and it stops. This is why the demand for Malaysia to choose an economic side misreads the country.
Putrajaya ensures that no single partner becomes indispensable because a supplier that cannot be replaced can dictate the terms. Diversification is not neutral. This is how a middle power preserves its bargaining position.
At the Asia-Pacific Roundtable on July 2, Anwar said Malaysia's foreign policy would remain fiercely independent and non-aligned, yet insisted the country could not be neutral on Palestine, Islamophobia, or its own sovereignty, "even when it comes to powerful partners like China and the United States".
Washington may find this uncomfortable; a relationship with institutional depth can absorb disagreement in its rhetoric without passing it on to its strategy.
The same logic applies to security. In October 2025, Malaysia and the United States signed a Memorandum of Understanding on Defence Cooperation and renewed their Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement, deepening a defence relationship that has developed over more than four decades; importantly, the arrangement did not establish a permanent American military presence.
That same month, Malaysia and China conducted the Aman Youyi 2025 exercise, including maritime-security activities in the Strait of Malacca.
Read as design, it is precisely what Malaysia wants: several major powers contributing to regional stability, none dictating the order of things. Cooperation is not an alliance, and Malaysia guards this distinction.
As great-power competition intensifies, the space for ambiguity narrows. The answer is to anchor the strategy, not abandon it: Anwar's insistence that some areas are non-negotiable gives both partners red lines that they can read in advance.
The recent frictions were not symptoms of a failing relationship but the ordinary weather of a mature one.
RIZAL HAMDAN
Senior Programme Officer,
Merdeka Centre

Title: Malaysia's trade hits record RM364.7bil in July as exports soar 38pct, surplus stretches 75 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's trade hit a record monthly high in July, rising 37.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM364.74 billion, driven by strong growth in both exports and imports.
The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said exports increased 38 per cent YoY to a record RM193.60 billion, while imports grew 36.4 per cent to RM171.14 billion.
This resulted in a trade surplus of RM22.46 billion, extending Malaysia's surplus streak to 75 consecutive months since May 2020.
The ministry said export growth was broad-based across manufactured, agriculture and mining goods, with electrical and electronic (E&E) products remaining the main driver.
E&E exports reached a record monthly value, increasing by RM32 billion from July 2025 on robust demand for semiconductors and other high-value E&E products.
Exports of metalliferous ores and metal scrap, as well as palm oil and palm oil-based agriculture products, also recorded higher shipments.
Malaysia's key markets also registered strong growth, with exports to Asean, China, the US, Taiwan and the European Union posting double-digit increases.
Exports to Asean, China and Taiwan reached their highest monthly values, while shipments to several free trade agreement (FTA) partners, including Mexico, Japan, the UK, Turkiye, Canada, Peru and Chile, also increased.
For the January-July period, total trade rose 24.7 per cent YoY to RM2.16 trillion, surpassing the RM2 trillion mark two months earlier than in 2025.
Exports increased 29.2 per cent to RM1.165 trillion, exceeding RM1 trillion a month earlier than last year, while imports rose 19.8 per cent to RM994.71 billion.
The trade surplus for the first seven months stood at RM170.50 billion, more than double the surplus recorded in the same period last year.
The ministry said trade, exports, imports and the trade surplus all registered record cumulative values for the January-July period.
It said sustained trade activity had also supported Malaysia's gross domestic product growth of six per cent in the second quarter of 2026, alongside resilient domestic spending and solid export growth.
"Despite persistent headwinds from global trade uncertainties, sustained trade activity has continued to support the expansion" of gross domestic product," it added.
The ministry said geopolitical shifts, tariff measures and supply chain realignments would continue to reshape global trade.
This requires Malaysia to diversify its export markets and products, maximise the use of FTAs and deepen engagement in high-potential markets.

Title: Ranhill's valuation running ahead of fundamentals – Analysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The valuation of Ranhill Utilities Bhd is running ahead of its fundamentals, said BIMB Securities, as it expects the Johor water utilities operator's core earnings to decline 27.6 per cent year-on-year in the financial year ending June 30, 2027 (FY27F).
As such, BIMB Securities had downgraded Ranhill to "Sell" from "Hold", despite raising its target price (TP) to RM2.39, from RM1.94, as the group trades at 30.1 times price-earnings ratio (PER), a substantial premium to its historical mean trailing PER of 17.2 times.
"We view the current valuations as demanding given our expectation for core earnings to decline 27.6 per cent Y-o-Y in FY27F as water margins normalize from FY26's elevated levels.
"While we remain positive on Ranhill's longer-term exposure to Johor's rising water demand and infrastructure expansion, we believe the recent share price re-rating has increasingly priced in these structural catalysts ahead of their earnings contribution," said BIMB Securities.
This view is also shared by MBSB Research in a note on Thursday. The research firm downgraded Ranhill to "Neutral" from "Buy" albeit with a higher sum-of-the-parts derived TP of RM2.84 from RM2.56.
"While we remain positive on Ranhill SAJ's longer-term earnings prospects, underpinned by rising water demand, we believe much of these positives have increasingly been reflected in the share price following the recent rally.
"We expect Ranhill SAJ to continue contributing strongly to the group's earnings moving forward, attributable due to the growth of data centres in Johor and the upcoming economic growth prospects from the Johor-Singapore SEZ and Special Financial Zone," stated MBSB Research.
Ranhill SAJ Sdn Bhd, the water operator of Johor, is 80 per cent owned by Ranhill. The increasing water demand in Johor fueled by demand from data centres as well as industrial and economic expansion will benefit Ranhill SAJ in the long run.
However, the water sector is a highly regulated business, which could limit the extent of the economic benefit that Ranhill SAJ could derive from the growth in demand, note BIMB Securities.
"We continue to expect Ranhill SAJ to benefit structurally from rising Johor water demand and longer-term capacity expansion but believe the regulated nature of the business limits the extent to which recent profitability can be extrapolated," BIMB Securities.
Ranhill Utilities recorded a core net profit of RM70.1 million for the fourth quarter of FY26, up 20 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
The improvement was supported by exceptional items, including the recognition of a RM48.9 million non-revenue water incentive grant, partly offset by a RM13.9 million impairment of business development costs for Ranhill Sabah Energy III Sdn Bhd (RSEIII)
BIMB Securities said it remains positive on Ranhill Utilities' long-term prospects, as Johor's expanding industrial base, JS-SEZ development and continued data-centre investments are expected to drive treated-water demand and spur the need for additional water infrastructure.
"The transition into Operating Period 7 should also provide greater clarity on Ranhill SAJ's medium-term capital expenditure and capacity-expansion programme," it said.
MBSB Research said it maintained its FY27 earnings forecast despite FY26 results coming in slightly below expectations, as the shortfall does not indicate a change in the group's underlying earnings trajectory.
"We expect continued water-demand growth in Johor, supported by the upcoming JS-SEZ, rising data centre consumption and the broader multiplier effects from incoming industrial and commercial investments," it said.
Ranhill was trading at RM2.65 before the noon break, down by 12 sen or 4.33 per cent from Wednesday's closing price of RM2.77, valuing the group at RM3.44 billion. The counter has rallied by more than 55 per cent so far this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ecuador intel chief, five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash
Article:
NAIROBI: Ecuador's intelligence chief and five US citizens died when a tourist helicopter crashed in central Kenya on Wednesday, killing all seven people on board, officials said.
The accident happened Wednesday morning in Samburu County, north of the capital Nairobi, according to the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA).
The aircraft had departed from the Loisaba wildlife reserve.
Images shared by the Kenya Red Cross on X in the afternoon showed a crash site in flames. It said difficult terrain hampered rescue operations.
"There were seven people on board the helicopter, one pilot and six passengers," Fredrick Kabunge, director of the Aircraft Accident Investigation Department (AAID), told AFP, confirming that no one had survived.
Contacted by AFP Wednesday evening, Samburu County police chief David Nkoroi said "operations have been suspended until tomorrow because of darkness and the complex nature of the ground and the scene of the crash."
Ecuador's Transport Minister Roberto Luque said the Latin American nation's intelligence chief Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife were among those killed.
"Today Michele and Stephany left us too soon. Thinking of their family, especially their children and parents," Luque wrote on X.
Sensi-Contugi, 42, is a former businessman appointed as head of Ecuador's National Intelligence Center in 2024.
He was a close associate of Ecuador's right-wing President Daniel Noboa, who has made his country a key US partner in Washington's renewed combat against drug cartels.
A US State Department spokesperson said that five American citizens died in the crash, without providing their identities.
Spanish-language broadcaster Telemundo however announced that one of its senior managers in Florida, Jose Alberto Suarez, had died in the crash.
"We are heartbroken to learn the tragic news that Jose was killed in a helicopter accident in Kenya," said a statement by Cesar Conde, newsgroup chairman of parent-company NBCUniversal, and two other executives.
"Jose was an exceptional colleague who cared deeply about his teams, the communities they served and the important role our stations play in people's lives."
Kabunge said the "helicopter was transporting tourists for a scenic flight."
In a video shared on X, black smoke could be seen billowing into the sky at the foot of Mount Ololokwe, where the crash occurred.
Mount Ololokwe is a sacred mountain for the Samburu people, its summit rising 2,000 metres above sea level, and it is a popular hiking destination. Companies offer helicopter flyovers.
The cause of the crash has not yet been established, with KCAA saying investigations were underway.
In March, a helicopter crash in western Kenya killed six people, including a member of parliament.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Son honours father who worked 25 years as a cleaner to support family
Article:
KAJANG: "Since I was young, I have never been ashamed of my father's job as a cleaner. In fact, I am proud because it is noble work," said 25-year-old Mohamad Zulfithri Mohd Johari.
Zulfithri, who now works as an executive officer at a ministry, recently gained attention online after sharing a convocation photo with his mother, Hasmawati Abdul Hamid, 50, and his father, Mohd Johari Shafie, 51, on TikTok.
In the post, he expressed his gratitude and paid tribute to his father's sacrifices on his birthday, stating that he would not have achieved success without his father's hard work as a cleaning staff member at the Gunung Semanggol Rest and Service Area (R&R) in Perak.
"My father has worked at the R&R for 25 years and still earns a living there today. He also took on side jobs, like repairing motorcycle tyres, to earn extra income.
"In the past, he collected aluminium cans and even took salary advances to support our family. Bringing me to his workplace and watching him clean the R&R are unforgettable memories for me," Zulfithri told Harian Metro.
The New Media Communication graduate from Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia (USIM) described his father as a quiet yet firm parent whose advice inspired him to excel academically.
"My father always told me to study hard because he and my mother did not have the opportunity to do so. Those words drove me forward, especially as the eldest child and the family's main hope," he said.
During his university days, Zulfithri served as the Student Representative Council (MPP) president, which allowed him to travel to Turkiye and South Korea.
At his convocation on Nov 25 last year, he received a leadership award on stage, a moment he cherished for bringing pride to his parents.
Zulfithri hopes to bring greater comfort to his family and eventually bring his parents to perform the pilgrimage in Mekah.
"To everyone out there, never be ashamed of your parents' jobs. Every job is noble as long as it is beneficial and provides an honest, halal source of income," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NASA satellite rescue mission fails
Article:
WASHINGTON: A complicated mission to save a NASA satellite from burning up in the atmosphere has failed, the US space agency said Wednesday, as the rescue spacecraft could not be controlled.
The Swift space telescope, which studies the most powerful explosions in the universe, will now likely plunge back to earth and disintegrate along the way later this year.
The unprecedented US$30 million dollar mission attempted to send a robot to grab the telescope and move it farther into orbit.
"This is not the outcome we were working toward, but it does not change why this mission was worth attempting," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said.
Planners had hoped the mission would pave the way for giving other satellites a second life.
"The team moved with extraordinary speed to give Swift a chance to carry out more science while advancing capabilities America will need for satellite servicing in the future," Isaacman added.
Developed by American startup Katalyst, the unmanned spacecraft was launched on July 3 by a small rocket named Pegasus, which was itself launched from an airplane.
However, on July 28 the company said the spacecraft had been in an out-of-control spin for 72 hours with multiple problems including a loss of communications.
In announcing the mission failure on Wednesday, Katalyst cited "ongoing attitude control issues" as the reason it and NASA were calling it off.
NASA said that the spacecraft would still attempt to reach the Swift telescope with the hope of giving scientists and engineers lessons for similar future missions.
The agency launched Swift in 2004 to study gamma-ray bursts.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New RM20mil motorsport circuit in Perlis to boost border tourism
Article:
PADANG BESAR: The RM20 million motorsport circuit under construction at the Chuping Valley Industrial Area (CVIA) is expected to boost Perlis' economy and border tourism by attracting motorsport enthusiasts from Malaysia and Thailand.
Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah said the 1.3km circuit would serve as a new tourism attraction while supporting local businesses and the wider state economy.
He said the facility, being developed in collaboration with ESR Motors, was also envisioned as a benchmark for motorsport development in neighbouring countries and the wider Asian region.
"A groundbreaking ceremony for the circuit will be held on Sept 15," he said after visiting the construction site here yesterday.
Abu Bakar said the circuit was expected to draw more Thai visitors, particularly motorsport enthusiasts, who could also spend on accommodation, food and other goods and services in Perlis.
"This will support the local economic chain and benefit traders," he said.
He added that the state government was also seeking potential investors to develop a five-star hotel in Perlis.
As part of efforts to strengthen border tourism, the state government also plans to engage with the Brunei and Thai governments on a twin-city concept involving Perlis-Brunei and Perlis-Bangkok.
Abu Bakar said no official meetings had been scheduled yet, but the state planned to make working visits to both countries to explore the initiative.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BMI raises 2026 average CPO price forecast to RM4,453 on tight supply
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BMI, a Fitch Solutions company, has raised its 2026 average price forecast for front-month crude palm oil (CPO) futures listed on Bursa Malaysia to RM4,453 per tonne, up from RM4,300 per tonne forecast it had maintained since October 2025.
In its latest Palm Oil Price Forecast report, BMI said this represents a year-on-year (y-o-y) 4.1 per cent rise from the 2025 average of RM4,279 per tonne.
"On a quarterly basis, following averages of RM4,177 per tonne in the first quarter (1Q) and RM4,504 per tonne in 2Q, we expect prices to average RM4,550 per tonne in 3Q and RM4,582 per tonne in 4Q," it said.
As of the Aug 17 market close, front-month Bursa Malaysia-listed palm oil settled at RM4,589 per tonne, a year-to-date gain of 16.1 per cent and a year-to-date average of RM4,380 per tonne, said BMI.
"The upward revision reflects a tightening near-term balance and a narrowing production surplus over 2026/2027.
"Broadly flat global output, held back by a 3.5 per cent decline in Malaysian production, is set against a consumption growth of 2.7 per cent, driven largely by Indonesia's accelerating biodiesel programme, which will divert additional palm from the export market into the domestic fuel pool," it added.
BMI also said it has revised down Malaysia's palm oil production forecast and expects output to ease 3.5 per cent y-o-y to 19.5 million tonnes in the 2026/2027 season.
Quoting Malaysian Palm Oil Board's latest monthly data, BMI said domestic output reached 1.8 million tonnes in July 2026, up 9.4 per cent month-on-month in line with seasonal expectations, but was 1.1 per cent below July 2025 levels, which reinforces BMI's recent downward revision.
Elevated stockpiles and strong first-half production support Malaysia's overall supply position, with January-June output at nine million tonnes, up 0.6 per cent y-o-y.
"Domestic stocks have drawn down over the course of the year. CPO closing stocks fell to 1.4 million tonnes in July from 1.7 million tonnes in January, driven by robust exports. CPO stocks still stand 40 per cent ahead of last year.
"Hence, although ongoing production challenges in Malaysia will lend support to global prices, the elevated stock position will temper the upside," said BMI.
On Malaysia's efforts to increase the national biodiesel blend rate up to 15 per cent, BMI said the impact on domestic CPO demand is expected to be relatively modest.
"We assume that a 12 per cent blend rate is the more realistic assumption for 2026, given that we are already halfway through the year with limited evidence of full implementation of the higher B15 mandate," it said.
BMI estimated that moving from the current B10 level to a full B15 blend will lift biodiesel-related CPO demand by about 200,000 to 270,000 tonnes on an annualised basis, which is a fraction of the domestic consumption forecast of 4.3 million tonnes for 2026/2027.
It is unlikely to reach the full 15 per cent blend this year with half the year gone.
"We therefore view the biodiesel mandate as a modest, gradual tailwind for domestic consumption rather than a step-change that would meaningfully alter our price outlook," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five held over upside-down Jalur Gemilang, Johor flags in state
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Five people have been arrested as police investigate three separate cases involving the Jalur Gemilang and Johor state flags flown upside down across the state.
Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said investigation papers had been opened in Kulai, Iskandar Puteri and Johor Baru South.
Completed investigation papers will be referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers (AG-C) for further action.
"We have three cases so far and investigations have been opened into all three. Arrests were made and investigations are ongoing.
"Once the investigation papers are completed, we will refer them to the AG-C for a decision on prosecution," he told a press conference at the Johor police contingent headquarters here today.
Hoo said two people — a 34-year-old foreign man and a 48-year-old Malaysian woman — were detained in Kulai, while two men aged 25 and 43 were arrested in Johor Baru South.
In Iskandar Puteri, police detained a 56-year-old man.
All five detainees were employees at the respective premises involved.
Hoo stressed that responsibility did not end once a flag was put up, urging premises owners, supervisors, and those tasked with displaying flags to ensure the flags were properly installed.
"Supervision must be carried out. What we see in these flag installation issues is that the workers are usually foreigners who do not know better.
"As the owner or person responsible for installing the flags, you should show them how to do it correctly.
"After installation, at the very least, supervision should be carried out, such as taking photographs and sending them to the supervisor responsible to check whether they have been installed correctly," he said.
In Kulai, a factory in the Indahpura Industrial area was ordered to close temporarily on Monday after the Malaysian and Johor flags were displayed upside down.
A Nepalese security guard and a
Malaysian woman linked
to the premises were remanded for four days to assist in the investigation.
The latest case was
detected at a factory
in the Southern Industrial and Logistics Clusters (SILC) in Gelang Patah, Iskandar Puteri.
The premises were subsequently ordered to close after checks revealed it was also operating without a valid business licence from the Iskandar Puteri City Council.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australia jobless rate hits near 5-year high of 4.5pct in July
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian employment unexpectedly fell in July and the jobless rate hit its highest point since late 2021, data showed on Thursday, adding to signs of a cooling labour market and easing pressure for another interest rate hike.
The report sent the Australian dollar down 0.2 per cent to US$0.7111. Markets are pricing in little chance of a rate hike from the Reserve Bank of Australia next month, but a move by the end of the year is still viewed as a coin toss, with much riding on inflation outcomes.
Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed net employment fell 15,800 in July from June when it jumped a revised 80,300. That was compared with a forecast for an increase of 15,000, though full-time jobs did rise by 16,300.
The jobless rate ticked up to 4.5 per cent, above a forecast of 4.4 per cent and running ahead of the RBA's expectation that it will be at 4.5 per cent by the end of the year. The monthly jobs data, however, have been volatile and past increases have been revised.
"Today's data are a touch weaker than the bank had pencilled in and, together with yesterday's softer wage growth, keep the pressure off the RBA to hike anytime soon," said Ben Udy, lead economist for Oxford Economics Australia.
The details of the report were on the soft side. The participation rate eased to 66.9 per cent from 67 per cent, hours worked dropped 0.6 per cent and the underemployment rate - a measure of slack in the labour market - held at a two-year high of 6.4 per cent.
The RBA has judged that the labour market has eased a little, one reason that it held policy rates steady at 4.35 per cent last week after three rate increases this year. On Wednesday, data showed that wages rose at a moderate pace for a fifth straight quarter.
Policymakers, however, warn that further tightening cannot be ruled out if inflation risks materialise, citing the US-Israeli war on Iran, the global artificial intelligence boom and poor productivity that has restrained the Australian economy's potential growth rate.
"The bigger risks are coming from offshore," said Krishna Bhimavarapu, an economist at State Street, adding that bond yields are rising, financial conditions are tightening and an El Nino event might affect Australia's wheat harvest.
"The risk is that adverse weather becomes an unwelcome inflation shock at a time the economy is under transition, potentially slowing the disinflation process and adding another layer of uncertainty to growth," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CK Hutchison seeks over US$1.5 billion from Panama over port takeover
Article:
HONG KONG: Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison said on Thursday it has filed international arbitration proceedings against Panama over its cancellation of a concession to operate two ports in the Panama Canal.
The dispute stems from a Panama supreme court ruling in January that struck down the contract that let Panama Ports Company (PPC), a unit of CK Hutchison, manage the canal's Pacific port of Balboa and the Atlantic port at Cristobal.
The decision came after claims by US President Donald Trump that China effectively ran the canal, part of broader tensions between Washington and Beijing.
On Thursday, the company said it had launched international arbitration proceedings against Panama over "breaches of an investment protection treaty" that culminated in the cancellation of the concession and takeover of the two ports.
"The Company is seeking damages of more than US$1.5 billion for the destruction of the Company's investments in Panama," the firm's board of directors said in a filing to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
"The Board strongly disagrees with the measures taken by Panama in violation of the treaty. The Company will continue to seek resolution with Panama while pursuing to the utmost all of the Company's rights and remedies under the treaty and international law."
Its subsidiary Panama Ports Company had filed a lawsuit opposing the suspension of its Panama Canal operations in February, and announced a month later it was seeking at least US$2 billion in damages.
The PPC will continue to pursue its own distinct rights under the separate arbitration, the board added.
The Panama Canal, which connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, handles about 40 per cent of US container traffic and five per cent of world trade.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK threatens sanctions as Israel advances West Bank settlement plan
Article:
LONDON: Britain said on Wednesday it had summoned Israel's charge d'affaires and demanded a halt to a major West Bank settlement project after Israeli authorities opened bidding for more than 1,200 homes in the area.
The E1 plan, green-lit by Israel last year, has drawn international condemnation, with the UN secretary general saying at the time that it posed an "existential threat" to a contiguous Palestinian state.
The project would further separate east Jerusalem, occupied and annexed by Israel and predominantly inhabited by Palestinians, from the West Bank.
British foreign minister Ed Miliband called the move "an unacceptable and destructive act" and said it would "endanger the viability of a two-state solution."
"The Israeli Government must halt E1 plans immediately, retract the tender and stop all settlement expansion," Miliband said in a statement.
Miliband said he delivered the message directly to his Israeli counterpart Gideon Saar and that Israel's charge d'affaires was summoned to the foreign ministry.
The British government also pledged to unveil "a comprehensive set of measures" in the coming weeks, including sanctions targeting people involved in the "illegal settlement expansion."
"Britain will not stand back and accept the destruction of the two state solution," Miliband said.
Israel approved the plans for the roughly 12-square-kilometre parcel of land known as E1 just east of Jerusalem, in August last year.
The plan seeks to build around 3,400 homes on the ultra-sensitive tract of land, which lies between Jerusalem and the Israeli settlement of Maale Adumim.
The latest tender covers more than 1,200 housing units, according to Israeli NGO Peace Now.
Peace Now said Israel's housing ministry published the tender on August 18 and immediately opened it for bids.
Submissions are due by October 19, one week before Israeli elections scheduled for October 27.
The group said the homes accounted for about one-third of the planned E1 development and accused the government of trying to advance construction commitments before the vote.
Israel heavily restricts the movement of West Bank Palestinians, who must obtain permits from authorities to travel through checkpoints to cross into east Jerusalem or Israel.
Last year, Britain and France were among 21 countries who condemned Israeli approval of the E1 project, calling it a violation of international law and urging Israel to reverse the decision.
Excluding east Jerusalem, the West Bank is home to around three million Palestinians, as well as about 500,000 Israeli settlers.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cabinet approves 17 measures, six quick wins to tighten KLIA, border security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Cabinet has approved 17 recommendations to strengthen security controls, screening and risk management at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and the country's international entry points.
The recommendations, contained in a joint memorandum by the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry, were approved yesterday.
In a statement today, the Home Ministry said six measures had been identified as immediate priorities, including targeted, risk-based screening of flights, passengers, crew and baggage deemed to pose risks.
The
move follows the arrest
of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia last month for allegedly smuggling drugs into the country.
"Among the measures are strengthened e-vetting and access control procedures for flight crew, airline employees, ground-handling personnel, airport operator employees, vendors, contractors and others requiring access to restricted security areas.
"Drug screening for aviation personnel, including pilots, cabin crew and relevant staff, will also be strengthened through pre-employment, periodic and random checks.
"Police presence at strategic locations will also be increased as a preventive measure, supported by additional General Operations Force personnel assigned to each shift at KLIA's Terminal 1 and Terminal 2," it said.
The ministry said security and intelligence information-sharing through the National Immigration Command Centre (NICC) would also be strengthened.
A Home Ministry-Transport Ministry Technical Committee, jointly chaired by the secretaries-general of both ministries, would also be established immediately to coordinate actions, resolve cross-agency issues and monitor implementation of the plan.
The ministry said the six measures would be prioritised for short-term implementation as part of a comprehensive action plan to strengthen the integrity of security controls at KLIA and the country's international entry points.
KLIA will serve as the pilot location before the plan is gradually expanded to other international entry points based on threat levels, operational requirements and the suitability of each location.
On July 28, the 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta after authorities seized 15 packets containing about 70,000 capsules of ecstasy and methamphetamine, weighing about 25kg and estimated to be worth RM45 million.
Indonesian police revealed that the pilot had been promised RM50,000 to act as a courier for the shipment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lim Lip Eng accuses police of double standards over flag incidents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng has accused police of applying double standards in their handling of two flag-related incidents involving a factory in Johor and the Kuala Terengganu City Council.
Lim said a Nepali security guard and a local woman in Kulai were detained and
remanded for four days
after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flags were displayed upside down.
"Neither had a criminal record, and both tested negative for drugs," he said in a statement today.
Lim said there was no evidence, based on information made public so far, that the pair had deliberately insulted the flags or disseminated the photograph.
He said police invoked several legal provisions, including those under the Penal Code and Communications and Multimedia Act.
"By contrast, when a Jalur Gemilang without the crescent and star was displayed at Dataran Batu Buruk under the responsibility of the Kuala Terengganu City Council, the explanation of a 'technical error' was accepted.
"The flag was simply replaced, with no reports of police arrests or remand," he said.
Lim questioned why the two people in Kulai were arrested and remanded while the government agency involved in the Terengganu incident was only required to provide an explanation.
"If immigration issues were the reason for detaining the security guard, why was the local woman also remanded?" he asked.
Lim also urged Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to explain the police's actions based on the facts and the law.
He said police should not take a hard line against ordinary people while remaining silent when negligence involved government authorities.
"If he fails to provide a reasonable explanation, he should consider resigning.
"If even a simple case involving the incorrect display of a flag cannot be handled fairly, how can he lead the police in tackling complex cases involving murder, corruption, syndicates and cybercrime?" he said.
On Aug 10, Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the installation of a Jalur Gemilang without its crescent and star symbols at Dataran Batu Buruk
was unintentional
.
He said the state government would investigate the matter and ensure it did not happen again, regardless of who installed it, including members of the public.
Meanwhile, Kuala Terengganu City Council mayor Lizan Che Mat said the Jalur Gemilang had originally featured the crescent and star symbols, but the section had become detached from its stitching.
He said the flag did not originally lack the symbols, but the section became detached due to strong winds that day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'More confrontational': Iran's new hardline security leadership
Article:
PARIS: Earlier this month Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei reshuffled Teheran's top security team, putting his own personal stamp on the appointments and readying the Islamic republic for a long-term confrontation with the United States.
Khamenei, in power since his father Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran in February, has yet to be seen in public since taking on the top job and his health and influence remain uncertain.
But on August 9 and 10 he filled key security posts – many of which became vacant after previous incumbents were killed in the war – with loyal, veteran figures hailing from the Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), Iran's ideological army, which has a long history of antagonism with the US.
They included Mohsen Rezaei, 71, a former commander of the IRGC for almost all the 1980s war against Saddam Hussein's Iraq and Hossein Taeb, 63, a former Guards intelligence chief who stepped down in mysterious circumstances in 2022.
The appointments are "indicative of the adoption of a more risk-ready, confrontational stance", said Jason Brodsky, policy director of the US-based United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI) think tank.
"These appointments are demonstrative of Iran believing it will be in a wartime footing for the foreseeable future," he said, adding that Khamenei has brought back "the old guard" of the IRGC.
It remains to be seen where the appointments will leave diplomacy with the US, after the expiry of a 60-day deadline for an agreement. The talks have so far been led by parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf who has become seen as a less hardline figure.
Here AFP looks at the key figures in Iran's security apparatus:
- SUPREME NATIONAL SECURITY COUNCIL SECRETARY MOHSEN REZAEI
Commander of the Revolutionary Guards in the 1980s and 1990s, Rezaei has never been far from prominence, with his stern face and black beard a familiar presence for Iranians on TV.
His forays into mainstream politics have not been successful, with several failed presidential bids, and his sudden elevation to the key post once held by Ali Larijani, who was killed in the war, surprised some observers.
In April, he warned that Iran would sink American ships in the Strait of Hormuz if the United States decided to "police" the key shipping bottleneck and in June said every American attack would be met by a "deluge" of missiles.
A 2020 US sanctions designation said he is suspected of involvement in the 1994 attack against a Jewish community centre in Argentina.
- BASIJ COMMANDER HOSSEIN TAEB
Taeb, a cleric, was named commander of the Basij, the IRGC's vast youth militia, which has become notorious as an enforcer of security in Iranian neighbourhoods.
He had led the intelligence arm of the IRGC for almost one-and-a-half decades up until June 2022 when he was suddenly replaced.
Why he was forced out was never made clear, although his departure coincided with the leaking of details over an alleged plot to target Israelis in Turkey.
Long seen as close to Mojtaba Khamenei, Taeb's appointment is seen as a sign of the authorities' readiness to suppress any repeat of the mass protests that erupted in January this year.
"Taeb's appointment also reflects the Iranian establishment's fear of renewed unrest as the economic situation deteriorates, with the Basij likely to play a leading role in quashing future protests," said Brodsky.
- REVOLUTIONARY GUARDS COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF AHMAD VAHIDI -
A former interior and defence minister, Vahidi is the third commander-in-chief of Iran's ideological army in less than a year after his predecessor Mohammad Pakpour was killed on the first day of the war and Hossein Salami was killed during Israel's 12-day war against Iran in June 2025.
Possibly for this reason, Vahidi kept a very low profile in the war, making his first public appearance during the funerals of Ali Khamenei in July.
While several written statements had been issued in his name as IRGC commander, Mojtaba Khamenei's decree was the first explicit confirmation of his promotion.
In the wake of 2022 protests, the US sanctioned Vahidi, saying he is responsible for "the commission of serious human rights abuses."
- ALI ABDOLLAHI CHIEF OF GENERAL STAFF OF THE ARMED FORCES -
Ali Abdollahi had previously led the Khatam al-Anbiya, Iran's inter-branch central military command tasked with coordinating operations. His new post has the crucial responsibility of coordinating between the regular armed forces and the IRGC.
Relatively prominent during the war, he warned in June that if the United States attacks Iran again "it will receive a harsher response than before, and the flames of war, in addition to creating insecurity in the region, will become more widespread and far-reaching."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Housewife loses nearly RM40,000 in online job scam
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A housewife lost nearly RM40,000 after falling victim to an online job scam promising lucrative commissions.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the 36-year-old victim lodged a police report on Aug 19 after realising she had been duped.
He said the victim initially received a phone call on Aug 15 from an individual claiming to represent TikTok to verify her address.
"Following the call, the victim received a parcel at her home before being contacted again and asked to review the items in a WhatsApp group.
"For that first task, she received a RM3 commission," he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim was then offered further tasks promising higher commission returns, but was required to make advance payments to unlock her earnings.
He said the victim made five transactions to several different bank accounts totalling RM38,505 between Aug 15 and Aug 18.
"The victim was later informed that she had earned RM2,100 in rewards, but was told the funds were frozen and could only be withdrawn after making additional payments.
"Growing suspicious after being asked for more money, the victim realised she had been cheated and lodged a police report," he said.
Azli added that all job transactions were conducted online without any face-to-face meetings with the suspects, and the funds lost were from the victim's personal savings.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asian stocks rally as US Treasury steps in to ease bond fears
Article:
HONG KONG: Asian markets rallied Thursday after the US Treasury said it would "at least double" the amount of long-term bonds to push down borrowing costs, after they surged this week to near two-decade highs.
The surprise move provided a much-needed shot in the arm for investors worried about a spike in 10- and 30-year yields caused by the prospect of inflation staying elevated, government borrowing and possible Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
Soon after the announcement, US equities reversed losses to end higher while the dollar tumbled against its peers as traders breathed a sigh of relief following a fresh bout of selling.
Fears had been surging after the yield on a 30-year US Treasury on Tuesday hit its highest level since June 2007, before the global financial crisis.
"This is probably more about the signal the administration wants to send to the market than the size of the operation -- it's small potatoes vs the $40 trillion US government debt," wrote Neil Wilson at Saxo Markets.
"I see it as a very strong sign that the Treasury has decided higher US yields are unacceptable, and that the recent blowout in the long end is undesirable.
"Clearly, Donald (Trump) is not happy yields have blown out."
The positive mood boosted Asia, where tech firms -- which rely on debt to pay for their huge AI investments -- were pummelled Wednesday.
Seoul led the charge higher, having been the focus of selling pressure the day before.
The Kospi jumped more than six per cent at one point as chipmaker SK hynix rocketed more than 12 per cent, helped by Wednesday's announcement by the firm of a $29 billion share buyback aimed at soothing recent worries. Samsung climbed almost nine per cent.
Tech firms also helped Tokyo higher, while Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Wellington and Manila were also well up.
The dollar stabilised after sinking against its peers, while gold jumped back above $4,500 for the first time since early June.
"The key question now is whether the fall in yields can last. If oil prices remain elevated and concerns over US borrowing continue, pressure on the long end of the Treasury curve could return," said City Index's Fiona Cincotta.
Crude prices have been rising for the past two weeks as hopes for a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz fade -- the deadline for an agreement came up this week.
Washington's naval blockade on Iran's ports and Tehran's attacks on commercial ships continue, and Iran's armed forces warned Gulf countries against assisting the US military on Wednesday.
While both sides recently said messages were being exchanged, Trump on Tuesday insisted talks were off, taunting Iran with a social media post depicting the strait as a "NEW U.S. Territory".
Meanwhile, minutes from the Fed's July meeting showed many policymakers believe interest rate hikes will be necessary if inflation does not decline.
Three of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented from the majority decision to hold rates steady, instead calling for an increase.
They noted economic activity had continued to expand at a "solid pace", but business investment was concentrated in the AI industry.
Eyes are now on next week's annual meeting of central bankers, economists and finance chiefs at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where investors will be hoping for some idea about Fed boss Kevin Warsh's thinking on rates.
